assignments.title: Executive Security Risk Register
assignments.course: Applied Security Architecture and Threat Modeling
assignments.scenario: A fictional 80-person retailer uses a cloud inventory system, payroll, guest Wi-Fi and a shared file drive. The finance manager reports former employees with lingering access; the store manager reports unreliable backups. You have authorization to assess only the fictional descriptions.
tasks: List four business assets and an owner for each.
Describe three credible risks with threat, weakness and consequence separately.
Rank risks using likelihood and impact on a qualitative low/medium/high scale, explaining uncertainty.
Recommend two near-term controls and how management would verify completion.
Write a 200–350 word executive summary identifying tradeoffs.
assignments.reference: A good response distinguishes account lifecycle, recoverability and network segmentation; it does not invent evidence of a breach.

assignments.title: Help Desk Incident Triage Portfolio
assignments.scenario: Fictional employee reports that a company laptop cannot reach the company learning portal. Wi-Fi is connected, other staff can browse normally, and the problem began following a scheduled update. No real network access is provided.
tasks: Write five clarifying questions that avoid collecting passwords.
Draw or describe a troubleshooting decision tree from device connectivity through DNS and application response.
Identify three harmless observations and two potentially disruptive changes requiring approval.
Prepare a concise escalation ticket including facts, unknowns and business impact.
Design a verification step and rollback decision.
assignments.reference: Good answers avoid equating a failed ping with an offline host or blaming the update without confirmation.

assignments.title: Web Application Trust Boundary Review
assignments.scenario: A fictional course app sends browser requests to an API for grades. Identity is handled by a third-party authentication provider; course materials are public but individual grades are private.
tasks: Describe a browser-to-API-to-database data-flow diagram.
Identify authentication versus authorization responsibilities.
Explain why hiding a button does not protect a grade endpoint.
Propose an event log that records failures without passwords or session tokens.
Write a 250-word security review for the product owner.
assignments.reference: The API must evaluate rights to each requested student's record, regardless of browser state.

assignments.title: Supplier Fraud Decision Memo
assignments.scenario: A fictional finance department receives a plausible email asking to change a supplier's bank account before an urgent $45,000 payment. Sender display name matches a known vendor but the domain differs by one character.
tasks: Identify observable evidence versus assumptions.
Recommend an independent verification process and responsible roles.
Document how to preserve the message appropriately.
Create a decision memo comparing payment delay against fraud risk.
Suggest one process improvement and a metric for effectiveness.
assignments.reference: Verify through a previously established contact method, not a phone number supplied by the suspicious email.

assignments.title: Windows Host Security Baseline
assignments.scenario: A fictional Windows 11 shared computer has standard accounts for two residents, a separate administrator account, automatic updates enabled, and an unidentified startup application. No real computer should be modified.
tasks: Windows Host Security Baseline
Windows Administration and Security

A fictional Windows 11 shared computer has standard accounts for two residents, a separate administrator account, automatic updates enabled, and an unidentified startup application. No real computer should be modified.
Create a baseline table for accounts, updates, antivirus, firewall, backups and startup programs.
Explain what a standard account can and cannot administer.
Describe how you would inspect the startup app's publisher and installation history without running it.
Write a safe, permission-based troubleshooting plan including rollback.
Draft a 300-word report stating findings versus unknowns.

Calculate the /24 network address, broadcast address and conventional host range.
Draw the path from client through gateway and name resolution to the application.

A synthetic file `/home/student/report.txt` has mode 640 and owner student, group analysts. A service account needs read access to a different report but should not be administrator.
Explain owner, group and other permissions for mode 640.
Distinguish directory traversal rights from file read rights.
Propose a least-privilege way to let an authorized service read only its approved report.
Describe how you would document a permission change and reverse it.
Explain why examining the academy's simulated terminal does not prove real Linux proficiency.

assignments.title: Weekend Security Operations Capstone
assignments.scenario: An invented organization reports elevated login failures, a scheduled application deployment, and customer portal errors. You are assigned to review only the supplied synthetic logs.
tasks: Prepare a consolidated timeline and label every event by source and time zone.
Separate confirmed events from hypotheses and identify at least four missing facts.
Draft a triage decision tree with escalation thresholds and stop conditions.
Propose a minimal evidence-collection plan and privacy protections.
Write a 400–600-word executive incident update plus a technical appendix.
assignments.reference: The exercise is based only on fictional evidence. Clearly distinguish observations from assumptions, do not claim to have tested external systems, and describe the specific verification evidence needed before closing a finding.

assignments.title: Windows and Linux Access Governance Capstone
assignments.scenario: A fictional retailer operates Windows workstations and a Linux reporting service. Three employees changed departments and a contractor left, but the simulated access inventory has not been reviewed.
tasks: Build a role-to-resource matrix including standard, elevated and service accounts.
Identify four conflicts between actual access and approved business duties.
Define an offboarding and session-revocation checklist.
Write a safe change and rollback plan for correcting excessive permissions.
Prepare a formal audit memo with verification criteria and residual risk.
assignments.reference: The exercise is based only on fictional evidence. Clearly distinguish observations from assumptions, do not claim to have tested external systems, and describe the specific verification evidence needed before closing a finding.

assignments.title: Web and Cloud Trust Boundary Capstone
assignments.scenario: A fictional learning application serves public course pages and private grades from a cloud API. Synthetic tests show a student can request another student's grade using an altered identifier.
tasks: Draw a data-flow diagram identifying the browser, identity provider, API and database.
Describe exactly where authentication and per-object authorization checks belong.
Propose test cases for allowed and denied access with synthetic accounts.
Design privacy-aware event records and a remediation verification process.
Write a 500-word finding and a short product-owner recommendation.
assignments.reference: The exercise is based only on fictional evidence. Clearly distinguish observations from assumptions, do not claim to have tested external systems, and describe the specific verification evidence needed before closing a finding.

assignments.title: Ethical Hacking Lab Engagement Capstone
assignments.scenario: A training company authorizes a review of one isolated mock application and one disposable Linux virtual machine. Its production website and all neighboring networks are excluded.
tasks: Write a rules-of-engagement document naming scope, constraints and stop conditions.
Create an asset and data classification inventory from the supplied scenario.
Define three narrow, falsifiable security test hypotheses.
Develop an evidence log template and severity triage criteria.
Submit a final 400–600-word assessment report with remediation and retest plans.
assignments.reference: The exercise is based only on fictional evidence. Clearly distinguish observations from assumptions, do not claim to have tested external systems, and describe the specific verification evidence needed before closing a finding.

assignments.title: Systems and Networks Final Project
assignments.scenario: A fictional company has 192.168.30.0/24 for general staff, 192.168.40.0/24 for finance, and a course portal whose hostname intermittently fails. Only synthetic configuration and error records are available.
tasks: Create a labeled topology diagram with authorized traffic flows and trust boundaries.
Compute network and broadcast addresses for both /24 networks and distinguish conventional usable ranges.
Produce a fault tree for gateway, DNS, transport and application-level failures.
Prioritize five non-disruptive tests and state expected positive/negative results.
Write a technical incident report and a 300-word executive summary, including uncertainties and retest criteria.
assignments.reference: A strong submission identifies independent network layers and does not infer compromise from DNS failures alone.

assignments.title: Security Incident Analysis Final Project
assignments.scenario: Synthetic incidents include three failed sign-ins, one authorized password reset, elevated web errors after a software release, and an untested backup procedure. No evidence confirms malicious access.
tasks: Build a chronologically normalized evidence table with confidence labels.
Document at least three competing hypotheses and the specific evidence needed to check each.
Write a proportional detection, escalation and containment decision plan.
Define recovery verification tests, including a safely controlled backup restoration.
Prepare a 500–750-word incident briefing with risks, owners and unresolved questions.
assignments.reference: Do not claim an attacker, a breach, or successful recovery without corroborated evidence.

assignments.title: Authorized Security Assessment Final Project
assignments.scenario: An owner authorizes review only of a fabricated browser training app and disposable virtual laboratory. Its public production environment and all other devices are out of scope.
tasks: Write the formal scope, authorization, stop conditions and contact procedures.
Create a data-flow diagram showing authentication, resource authorization and logging.
Identify four synthetic test hypotheses, including intended success and denial cases.
Build a findings register with affected asset, observed evidence, likelihood/impact rationale, owner and safe remediation.
Deliver a 600–900-word professional assessment report and a specific verification/closure plan.
assignments.reference: A simulated result cannot certify a production system or real-world penetration-test proficiency.
